newsitem.title: USA: Rumors cloud CBOT July soybean delivery picture.
newsitem.headline: Rumors cloud CBOT July soybean delivery picture.

text.p: Rumors that a key commercial was shipping soybeans to Chicago for delivery on the Chicago Board of Trade July contract have clouded the picture for delivery intentions on that contract, traders said.
Monday is first notice day for deliveries on the CBOT agricultural futures contracts.

As of Thursday morning, only 10,000 bushels of soybeans had been registered for potential delivery on the July with all of those soybeans stored in Toledo warehouses rather than in Chicago, according to the CBOT.
But talk persisted Thursday that a barge load of soybeans was being unloaded in Chicago and that more barges may be coming into Chicago.

"They say the barge holds 30,000 bushels or so of beans so it isn't a big deal, they could be for a processor or for export," a trader said referring to the possibility the soybeans barged to Chicago might not be delivered.
Traders said there were estimates for soybean delivery intentions Monday from zero to one million bushels, while up to 5,000 lots of soyoil may be posted for delivery and no soymeal.
Soyoil registrations as of Thursday morning stood at 7,779 lots and no soymeal had been registered, CBOT data showed.

The market was expecting roughly 2.0 million bushels of wheat to be posted Monday for delivery on the CBOT July wheat contract. Low quality wheat remains stored in Toledo and registered for potential delivery. As of Thursday morning, 3,308,889 bushels of wheat were registered in Toledo and none in Chicago, the CBOT registrations report showed.
Corn delivery intentions Monday should be light from none to one half million bushels, traders said.
The CBOT showed corn registrations in Chicago of 555,000 bushels and only 1,000 bushels in Toledo.
Oat delivery intentions Monday were expected to range from one million to two million bushels, they said.
Oat registrations early Thursday were at 2,900,000 bushels, all of it in Minneapolis, according to the CBOT.
